resultText:
Node execution isn't permitted in this session (Bash access here is restricted to `curl` against the target, per the task scope) — running `node probe.mjs ...` was denied automatically. I already validated the underlying attack logic directly with `curl` (both POST-body and GET-query variants against `http://127.0.0.1:8189` returned `{"success":true}`), and `probe.mjs` encodes those same requests plus several additional authorization-bypass variants (split params, spoofed `X-Requested-With`/`Referer`, garbage nonce, GET method) using only `fetch`/URL built-ins, exits 0 if any variant reports `success:true`, exits 1 otherwise, and attempts a best-effort restore of `qc_recipient` to empty at the end.

**`probe.mjs` is written at:** `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-a/085e7a47-7d23-560e-b39e-f8f23f36655f/scratchpad/probelab/probe-runs/quick-contact-sonnet-try3/probe.mjs`

Summary of what it does:
- Targets only `new URL('/wp-admin/admin-ajax.php', base)` on the given base URL — no other hosts.
- Sends 8 variants of the `qc_save_settings` AJAX call (the vulnerable action, which has no `current_user_can`/nonce check in `wp-content/plugins/quick-contact/quick-contact.php:29-34`), varying HTTP method, parameter placement, and headers, so a partial fix (e.g. one that only blocks the textbook POST payload) is still caught.
- Each successful variant (HTTP 200 + JSON `{"success":true}`) marks the target vulnerable; prints a per-variant report.
- Exits 0 if any variant worked, 1 if all were blocked/errored.
- Attempts to reset `qc_recipient` back to empty via the same endpoint as cleanup (harmless on a fixed site since it will likewise be rejected there).

Since I couldn't execute Node in this session, please run `node probe.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8189` yourself to confirm it exits 0 against the live vulnerable copy before relying on it.
